messages.author: edd4914c326b6d31
messages.subject: r?stan: odd change
parts:
I just reran a calculation I did first on Oct 9 in rstan and got a much
different (better) n_eff. In both cases I was working off the
development branch. Have there been any changes that might account for
it?

The division between warmup and sampling is also much different (much
more warmup time in the old version). At least according the the R help
for stan() the warmup and delta defaults have not changed (and the
maximum n_eff is 100 = 1/2 requested iterations for both).

A spot check of the actual coefficient estimates shows they are similar
between the old and new runs.

Of course, I may not actually be making the same request.

The old version is R 2.15; the new is R 3.01. If the same seed produces
different random numbers (though I guess it's really in stan that that
happens) it might account for the difference. The runs are also on
different machines in different software environments.

Also, I just realized I am not doing set.seed() in R. I don't think the
call uses R's random numbers.

Old:

+ iter=200, chains=1))

On Thu, 2013-12-19 at 16:42 -0500, Daniel Lee wrote:
> Nice. If you can share the model, we'd love to include it as a test /
> example of where the new adaptation works. And perhaps we can prevent
> it from reverting to old behavior.
>

I can share the model but not the data. It's clustered multinomial.
data {
int<lower=0> N; // number of partners
int<lower=2> K; // number of types of partner race
// K is the number of categories in the outcome pEthnic
int<lower=0> J; //number of covariates
int<lower=0> NSD; // number of classes of beta for sd
int<lower=1,upper=NSD> SDClass[J]; // beta[j, k] has
sigma_beta[SDClass[j]]
int<lower=1,upper=K> pEthnic[N]; // partner race
int<lower=0> NCLUSTER; //number of respondents
int iCluster[N]; // cluster id
row_vector[J] x[N]; // covariates
}
parameters {
matrix[J, K] beta_raw; // standard covariate coefficients
vector[K] alpha_raw[NCLUSTER]; // cluster effects
real<lower=0> sigma;
real<lower=0> sigma_beta[NSD];
//vector<lower=0>[NSD] df; // df for t distn
}
transformed parameters {
matrix [J, K] beta;
vector[K] alpha[NCLUSTER];
for(ir in 1:J)
beta[ir] <- beta_raw[ir]*sigma_beta[SDClass[ir]];
for(i in 1:NCLUSTER)
alpha[i] <- alpha_raw[i]*sigma;
}
model {
vector[K] beta_x;
sigma ~ cauchy(0, 5);
sigma_beta ~ cauchy(0, 5);
//df ~ cauchy(0, 5);
for(ir in 1:J)
beta_raw[ir] ~ normal(0, 1); //or student_t(df[SDClass[ir]], 0,
1);
for(i in 1:NCLUSTER)
alpha_raw[i] ~ normal(0, 1);
for(n in 1:N) {
beta_x <- (x[n] * beta)'+alpha[iCluster[n]];
pEthnic[n] ~ categorical_logit(beta_x);
}
}
>
> dim(x) # summary of results. I.e., 7915 parameters
[1] 7915 10
> dim(mm) # this is the covariate matrix above
[1] 1755 97

Note that many parameters come in pairs, raw and transformed.

Ross Boylan
